To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most automatable and desirable aspects of healthcare work are related to the administration of healthcare, and the least automatable and undesirable aspects of healthcare work include the diagnosis of disease, treatment and rehabilitation, and the management of patients.
(1) 30% of healthcare work could be completely automated, (2) 50% of healthcare work should not be automated at all, and (3) 20% of healthcare work can be partially automated.

the majority (70%) of healthcare work is both automatable and desirable to automate, while 20% of healthcare work is neither automatable nor desirable to automate, and only 10% of healthcare work can be automated, but it should not be.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: “How can we ensure that automation technologies are used to the benefit of all stakeholders in healthcare?”
the question of what healthcare work should be automated and how to achieve this in practice.
the question of how to ensure that the automation of healthcare will not only be feasible, but also desirable and beneficial for all stakeholders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
automation should be applied where the potential for improvement is highest, and that this is the case for many tasks that are currently carried out by healthcare professionals.
, while there is a lot of work that could be automated, there is also a lot of work we do not want to automate.
the healthcare sector is not only ripe for automation but also that it is desirable to automate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
automation is not a panacea, but a tool to improve human life.
we provide a tool to support policymakers in developing practical strategies that harness the positive power in AI technologies while accompanying the change and empowering stakeholders.
automation technologies can help us to improve healthcare, but we need to be careful about how we use them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the automation of healthcare work is a complex task that requires a multidisciplinary approach, as well as the involvement of healthcare practitioners, policymakers, and experts.
automation technologies should be applied with care, and only to those tasks that are not only technically automatable but also desirable to automate.
automation technologies can help healthcare practitioners to do their work more effectively and efficiently.
